messages:
maria: Quick question — as we scale private control planes to thousands of customers, who should own the egress IPs for control-plane outbound traffic? control-plane VPC with shared NAT, or delegate SNAT to each customer endpoint VPC?
chris: I'm leaning shared NAT on the control plane side for observability and simpler TLS termination. But worried about per-customer isolation and IP exhaustion. :thinking:
kai: sharing simplifies billing/ingestion (single egress set to whitelist in partner firewalls). downside: you need enough public IPs and NAT capacity; AWS NAT gateway is $$$ if per-tenant.
lee: If we go per-customer SNAT we avoid IP reuse across tenants, but route tables and peering count blow up. Also cross-account peering across 5k accounts is unrealistic.
maria: Right — two other constraints: (1) customers often want to pin egress IPs for allowlists, (2) corporate customers need per-tenant audit trails in logs.
chris: Idea: hybrid -- use a small shared egress pool for low-tier tenants and reserve optional dedicated egress (per-tenant small NAT or Elastic IP) for enterprise. That reduces IP count and gives dedicated option.
kai: For the shared pool, we should allocate prefixes from our IPAM in /22 chunks and run a fleet of scaled NAT proxies with connection tracking. Prefer lighter-weight proxy (envoy sidecar egress nodes) instead of per-tenant NAT GW to control cost.
lee: Scaling note: if we naively gave /26 per tenant for dedicated endpoints, 5k tenants would need ~320k IPs (5k * 64) — too many. We need dynamic allocation or reuse.
maria: Agree. Also certificate rotation: when control plane rotates mTLS certs we need a clear handshake pattern so tenants don't need manual updates. Proposal: control plane rotates leaf certs frequently, but we keep a trust anchor per tenant that is long-lived. Then we do in-band rollover with a short overlap window.
chris: Also consider hairpin costs — if control plane egresses back to customer services over peering, hairpinning through NAT could double data path. Transit Gateway-based patterns might help but TGW attachment limits and cost matter.
kai: Quick config sketch for shared egress pool (for ops docs):
```
control_plane_egress:
  allowed_prefixes: ["172.31.200.0/22"]
  nat_backend: envoy-proxy-cluster
  per_customer_mode: optional-dedicated
```
lee: Ops concerns: IP rotation and allowlist changes are support tickets. We should support customer-facing UI to download current egress ranges and webhook notify on changes.
maria: Action items: (1) run cost/scale spike comparing shared envoy NAT pool vs per-tenant NAT gateways at 1k/5k/10k tenants, (2) draft mTLS rotation pattern with minimal customer ops, (3) prototype IPAM allocation strategy: dynamic per-tenant allocation + reuse TTL.
ops-bot: Created ticket NET-821: "egress-ip-strategy spike and mTLS rollover design" assigned to @maria, @kai, @chris — due in 2w. :white_check_mark:
chris: 👍 prioritizing the spike. I'll pull TGW/Peering cost matrix into the ticket.
maria: Thanks — keeping this thread as the design seed. If anyone has objections to hybrid model call it out now. :thumbsup:
